summary: No fundamentals thesis is broken by evidence in the files. Today's moves in the held names were small (DPZ -1.6%, CARG -1.5%, IDXX -0.8%, WMT -0.2%, FAST +1.5%) and are price noise, not accounting evidence. The menu in inputs/fundamentals.json is as of 2026-10-20 and shows no new filings, so every invalidation tied to fundamentals is untested: DPZ still has cfo $792M above net income $602M, IDXX cfo $1,182M above $1,059M, FAST cfo $1,296M above $1,258M (about 1.03x, thin as the PM noted), CARG cfo $295M against $156M, WMT cfo $41.6B against $21.9B. DPZ, IDXX, FAST, CARG and WMT were all on the 10-20 menu; VOO is a fund and is simply the one holding off the menu.
update: No lessons in learning.json apply to the fundamentals analyst (L1 is for proposer and portfolio-manager) and graded_calls is empty, so there is no track record to adjust from. Items to watch, none of them breaks: (1) DPZ's invalidation relies on a screen that reflects the Q3 results reported 10-13, but the menu data still uses the FY2025 10-K (fy_end 2025-12-28), so the next menu refresh should be checked for DPZ dropping off or cfo falling below net income. Its Consumer Staples top rank still partly reflects the wholesale-groceries SIC mislabel. (2) FAST has thin cash conversion and its gross margin test failed (gross_margin_improved false), so the first earnings report is the real test of its thesis. (3) CARG failed current_ratio_improved, has volatility 0.394 near the 0.438 cutoff and thin dollar volume; its fundamentals are strong but the position is a starter and should stay small. I am not recommending any trade.
